modelReview.summary: The negative binomial regression model was fitted with a default dispersion parameter (alpha=1.0) without estimation, invalidating standard errors and p-values. Additionally, the study lacks justification for model choice, adequate reporting of cohort and variables, and handling of missing data. These issues prevent any local interpretation of results.

findings.title: Negative binomial model used default dispersion parameter alpha=1.0 without estimation; standard errors and p-values may be invalid.
evidenceRefs: stats-run/stats-run.json: warnings field includes 'Negative binomial dispersion parameter alpha not set. Using default value alpha=1.0'
findings.whyItMatters: The negative binomial model's variance function depends on alpha; using a fixed alpha=1.0 assumes a specific dispersion that may not match the data, leading to incorrect inference.
findings.actionableFix: Re-fit the model using maximum likelihood estimation of alpha (e.g., statsmodels' discrete.NegativeBinomial) or method of moments, and report the estimated alpha and its standard error. Re-evaluate all results.
findings.deterministicVerification: Run the analysis script and check whether the negative binomial model object has an estimated alpha parameter (not fixed to 1.0). Confirmation can be obtained from the model summary or a dedicated dispersion estimate output.

findings.title: No evidence of overdispersion testing or model comparison (e.g., against Poisson) to justify negative binomial choice.
evidenceRefs: stats-run/diagnostics.json: no likelihood ratio test or dispersion statistic
findings.whyItMatters: Choosing NB to handle overdispersion is sensible, but the model should be justified by evidence of overdispersion. Without testing, model selection may be ad hoc, and the risk of model misspecification remains unexamined.
findings.actionableFix: Provide a formal test of overdispersion (e.g., likelihood ratio test of alpha=0, Pearson chi-square/df from a Poisson model, or dispersion test) and document the result. Alternatively, compare fit statistics with a Poisson model.

findings.title: Insufficient reporting of cohort construction, variable definitions, and missing data handling, hampering interpretability and reproducibility.
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md: Methods section mentions cohort definition 'read from available run artifacts' but no details; variables listed without definitions or coding; missingness only mentioned as 'complete-case'.
findings.whyItMatters: Without clear definitions, readers cannot assess internal/external validity, replicate the study, or evaluate confounding and selection bias.
findings.actionableFix: Add a table of baseline characteristics, define each variable (e.g., treatment: binary 0/1; age: in years; severity: scale and range; count_events: unit of time/observation). Describe eligibility criteria and the number of records excluded at each step. Clarify the complete-case strategy and any sensitivity analysis.

findings.title: Potential selection bias from complete-case analysis; missingness mechanism not examined.
findings.whyItMatters: If missingness is related to outcome or exposure, complete-case analysis yields biased estimates. The assumption of MCAR is often unrealistic.
findings.actionableFix: Report the number and percentage of missing values per variable, compare characteristics of complete and incomplete cases, and consider multiple imputation or inverse probability weighting if data are not MCAR. At minimum, discuss the potential direction of bias.

findings.title: Manuscript reports log rate ratios (estimates) but not rate ratios; rate ratios are more clinically interpretable.
findings.whyItMatters: Rate ratios facilitate understanding of effect size. Clinicians and public health readers expect rate ratios.
findings.actionableFix: Include rate ratios and their 95% CIs in the results table, alongside or instead of log-scale estimates.

findings.title: No data summary or description of distribution of outcome and covariates.
findings.whyItMatters: Cannot assess whether the outcome is truly count (non-negative integers), if it contains excess zeros, or if covariates have plausible ranges, all of which affect model appropriateness.
findings.actionableFix: Provide summary statistics (mean, median, min, max, variance, proportion zeros for count_events) and histograms or frequency tables. Report the distribution of age, severity, and treatment.

findings.title: Model diagnostic evaluation incomplete: no assessment of deviance residuals, influence measures beyond leverage/Cook's, or goodness-of-fit.
evidenceRefs: stats-run/diagnostics.json: no deviance or Pearson residual diagnostics, no dispersion test, no residual vs fitted plot analysis
stats-run/figure-qa.json: empty, no evaluation of the residual plot
findings.whyItMatters: Without these, the adequacy of the model fit cannot be confirmed. Residual patterns could indicate model misspecification.
findings.actionableFix: Compute deviance residuals, produce residual vs fitted plot and QQ plot of deviance residuals, check for overdispersion after proper alpha estimation, report goodness-of-fit statistics (e.g., Pearson chi-square/df).
